items.summary: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) is an open standard that lets AI agents from different vendors discover each other, delegate tasks and exchange results over HTTP.

items.title: Subagent
items.summary: A subagent is an AI agent that a lead agent spawns to handle one delegated task in its own context window, returning only a summary of its work to the parent.

items.title: Agent team
items.summary: An agent team is a group of AI agents that split one goal into tasks, claim work from a shared list and message each other directly, usually under a lead agent.

items.title: Tool calling
items.summary: Tool calling is how a large language model asks software to run a named function with structured arguments, letting AI agents query data and act elsewhere.

items.title: Agent memory
items.summary: Agent memory is storage that lets an AI agent keep facts, preferences and past actions across separate sessions, beyond a context window that resets each time.

items.title: Context window
items.summary: A context window is the maximum number of tokens an AI model can consider in a single request. How windows are counted, filled, compacted and why they degrade.

items.title: System prompt
items.summary: A system prompt is the standing instruction set a developer gives a language model before any user speaks. How it works, why it leaks, and its role in AI ads.

items.title: Agent skills
items.summary: Agent skills are folders of instructions, scripts and files, built around a SKILL.md file, that AI agents load only when a task needs specialised know-how.

items.title: Agent plugins
items.summary: Agent plugins are installable bundles of skills, connectors, commands, subagents and hooks that extend AI agents such as Claude Code, Cowork and OpenAI's Codex.

items.title: Powering the Agent Development Lifecycle with any framework, from ADK to LangChain and beyond
items.summary: The Agents CLI Extension System enables developers to use frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or custom enterprise stacks while retaining a unified deployment and evaluation workflow. It details a first-party LangChain template that scaffolds, runs, and deploys agents without requiring the Agent Development Kit (ADK). Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.
